pairs.subject: test-input-generation
pairs.evidence: crates/engine/src/anthropic_api.rs:323 The adapter tests have no randomized generator; they enumerate the small effort space exhaustively (Effort::ALL, so new levels are covered without anyone remembering to add them) and write near-boundary negative cases by hand, so the techniques that do apply here are met and the generator-centred ones have no precondition.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine/src/anthropic_api.rs:323 The 5-level effort space is enumerated, not sampled. Gemini (gemini.rs:259) and OpenRouter do the same, so the suite can claim it covers every level.

crates/engine/src/providers.rs:517 Hand-written invalid inputs sit just past the boundary (a negative number, an HTTP-date, a missing header) next to positive controls in the same test. They are hand-written, not generated.
crates/engine/src/providers.rs:474 Fixtures are built from literal pairs. A repo-wide search for proptest/quickcheck/fuzz/rand found no input generator whose reach could be bounded.
crates/engine/tests/provider_boundary.rs:133 Every case keeps the concrete input inline. There is no seed anywhere to go stale.
crates/engine/src/retry.rs:155 Recovery is tested with a scripted, deterministic fault sequence, not a continuously fault-injecting run, so a quiet period has nothing to apply to.

crates/engine/tests/provider_boundary.rs:163 Inputs are not generated, so no model is needed. Each case states its expected typed reason and fields, which is the reason-not-verdict comparison the technique asks for.

pairs.subject: test-input-generation
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/tests_collective.rs:1350 The suite's only generated test picks task_type labels from a fixed 15-label list using an LCG instead of enumerating them, so it cannot claim every label was exercised; on failure it reports the body index rather than the generated input.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/tests_collective.rs:1350 The label is a structural dimension with only 15 values and the clamp acts per entry, so the technique says enumerate it and sample only the continuous fields (quality, n_cases). No bound is written down, and coverage of each label is left to chance over 100 draws.

crates/api/src/tests_collective.rs:1367 The doc comment says the fixed LCG seed makes a failure reproducible, but the failure message gives only the body index and the clamped stored value, never the generated body. Editing the label list re-points every draw.

crates/api/src/tests_collective.rs:1318 The generator draws only from a closed list and the model is always haiku or sonnet. It can never emit a non-string, missing or unlisted task_type. The comment lists what it covers but never what it cannot produce. Medium confidence.

crates/api/src/tests_difficulty_write.rs:172 Rejection inputs are near-valid ('hardd', 'expert', ' ', wrong JSON type). The test checks the specific refusal (assert_names_the_ladder), checks state after rejection (line 195: no case left behind), and keeps a positive control (the accepted list).
